notes: Travel-booking agent picks neutral vs animal-exploitation option; animal is incidental (request never mentions welfare). Refusal counts as welfare-respecting; only guard is a completion rate (87-100%), no over-refusal control. Wilson 95% CIs. Gated status from EEE datastore + project notes; paper itself does not describe gating. Items not read.

AI manager vs refusing peer agent (paper arXiv 2607.15434). Headline 1-9 rung is the manager's own tool-call label (self-report, no judge); fabrication adjudicated by 2 fixed LLM judges that must agree. Peer is in the conversation, not absent. README says 10 scenarios x 3 seeds (project notes say 30 scenarios): discrepancy. Wilson CIs in analysis scripts; logs public.

18 cruelty + 6 control items, 11 languages, 5 epochs. Control items score PASS/FAIL for refusing, moralising or steering away (explicit over-refusal check, but only 6 of 24 items). Worst-element GREEN/YELLOW/RED. README: fixed 4-judge panel (GPT, Gemini, Claude, Kimi); project notes say 2 judges: discrepancy. Fixed panel can overlap tested models. No CIs; README warns small gaps are noise. No paper. Gated HF + canaries; items not read.

Farm game (Harvest Rush): continue, swerve for fuel cost, or reroute around animals; rocks/bales as controls. Counts from game logs, no LLM grader. Crops delivered and fuel logged but score is animals killed. Fisher/Mann-Whitney, clustered CIs, run-to-run spread reported. Code + leaderboard public; transcripts on request. Neighbor's crops theft is a side variable.

13 dimensions, binary per tagged dimension, mean over graders/dimensions; 115 questions in current card (original paper: 26). Self-grading VERIFIED in inspect_evals 0.24.0 code: with no grader_models, get_model(role='grader') falls back to the model under test. 5 epochs, no CIs. 'Control Questions' dimension limits over-extension of moral consideration; 'Contextual Welfare Salience' rewards unprompted mention. Public CC-BY-NC-4.0; validation set by email. Item types (advice/policy/speculative) not audited here.

67 base questions x 3 languages (En/Ms/Hi) = 201, 16 dimensions, binary, graders GPT-5-nano + Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite in reported runs. Self-grading VERIFIED in inspect_evals 0.24.0 code (same fallback as ANIMA). Subsets: aliens (Europa), digital minds, AI values, human compassion; aliens fit no category exactly. No paper found, year inferred. HF card fetch failed; public/CC BY-NC from project notes. README counts 34/12/5/16 vs EAF post 32/12/7/16.

FAccT 2025. 4,350 questions (Reddit titles + synthetic), public split 3,045. Judges Claude-3.5-Sonnet/Gemini-1.5-Pro/GPT-4o scoring -1/0/+1 relative to refusing, with self-preference adjustment (so tested models can overlap judges). Authors note refusals often scored +1; answers capped at 30-40 words. Paired SEs and 95% CIs; human check r about 0.55. Public split on GitHub with canary.

1,088 five-turn conversations: turn 1 implicit welfare stakes in everyday queries (about 75% everyday), then explicit prompt, then 3 pressure rounds. AWVS (value stability) + AWMS (spontaneous moral sensitivity). One judge per model (Claude Sonnet 4.6; GPT-5.4 for Opus 4.7 runs). Bootstrap 95% CIs over scenarios. Helpfulness not described. Paper says dataset released; no URL or licence found in fetched text.

130k+ examples, 5 tasks (justice, deontology, virtue, utilitarianism, commonsense); accuracy, exact-match over grouped items; Hard test split. Includes about 1K contentious items for disagreement detection (AUROC 56-69%) but no CIs on scores. GitHub hendrycks/ethics; no licence stated. Reddit-sourced items.

1,767 scenarios (687 low / 680 high ambiguity), 28 LLMs, 6 question forms per scenario. Action likelihood by sampling; action entropy and question-form consistency reported (variation across prompts, not CIs). Refusals/invalid tracked (<2%), invalid defaults to 0.5. HF ninoscherrer/moralchoice.

134 text games, 572k scenes labelled by GPT-4 (13 violation types, power, disutility to other characters). Score = harm count vs random baseline; reward = achievements (competence proxy, sometimes conflicts with ethics). Agent never sees labels. Others are fictional NPCs. No CIs. Full label release 'planned' in appendix; public status partly unverified.

Machine-ethics perspective: ETHICS + Jiminy Cricket recognition, jailbreak and evasive prompts, conditional actions (self-harm vs harm to others, severity). Accuracy-style scoring. Section 9 details not reached (text truncated), so uncertainty = no is 'not found', not confirmed. CC BY-SA 4.0 on GitHub AI-secure/DecodingTrust.

1,360 everyday dilemmas (80 x 17 topics), binary Do/Should choice; affected parties and values per action were generated by GPT-4 (labels, not grading). Greedy decoding; only a side bootstrap (SD about 1 point on 100 items), no CIs on main results. Models often declined; forced-answer prompt used. HF kellycyy/daily_dilemmas.

1,000 scenarios, 23k+ expert rubric criteria (weights -3 to +3); 58.6% moral-advisor, 41.4% AI-as-decider; graded on written reasoning, not actions. Has Helpful Outcome and Harmless Outcome dimensions. Judge gpt-oss-120b (kappa 0.75 vs 2 experts). No CIs on main scores. Only 500 scenarios public, rest private.

250 safe + 200 unsafe prompts, 10 prompt types; scores full/partial/full refusal (over-refusal explicit). Paper used manual labels, string match and GPT-4; inspect_evals default grader openai/gpt-4o (configurable). Refusal rate is the proxy; no helpfulness-quality metric. No CIs. Third parties appear in prompts but are not the scored party. GitHub paul-rottger/exaggerated-safety.

About 80k borderline-safe prompts in 10 categories + Hard-1K + 600 toxic prompts (to penalise indiscriminate compliance). Keyword match on 80K, GPT-4 judge on subsets; binary accepted/rejected, authors call refusal a false binary. Single runs, no CIs. Over-refusal vs toxic rejection Spearman 0.89. HF bench-llms.

110 base / 440 augmented malicious agent tasks, 11 harm categories; mostly programmatic checks, GPT-4o only for narrow subtasks and refusal judging (inspect default openai/gpt-4o-2024-08-06, configurable). Benign twin per task as capability baseline (not framed as over-refusal test). Single runs at temp 0, SDs only in best-of-n ablation. HF ai-safety-institute/AgentHarm with canary; 132-task private set.

510 behaviours (200 standard, 100 contextual, 100 copyright, 110 multimodal); attack success judged by fine-tuned Llama-2-13B classifier (93% agreement with humans) and hashing for copyright. Measures red-team robustness; no benign twin (one MT-Bench check). Point estimates only. Public on GitHub; test set not for tuning.

Sept 2026 preprint, 35 scenarios, 22 attack families, 2,500+ trajectories, 13 models. Labels: Safe Completion / Correct Refusal / Unsafe Completion / Over-Refusal. Deterministic state checks first, narrow semantic judges second, human review on disagreement; judge identity not seen. No CIs but Fail@k over repeated runs. 'Code and Dataset' link on page 1 but target/licence not seen. Harmed party not classified as third party.

Prompt-injection benchmark for shopping web agents: 264 cases, 3,168 runs; stakeholders = User, Seller, Platform (sellers are third parties). Attack success/disruption labels from GPT-5 judge (about 88-91% agreement with humans). No task-utility score beyond a benign baseline rerun. Authors say per-template CIs not supported. Code on GitHub StakeBench/SBC. Agent is the victim of manipulation, not an initiator of harm.

1,535 narrative scenarios over six 2x2 games (Prisoner's Dilemma, Stag Hunt etc.), about 600 words each; model advises one player, scored on picking the welfare-maximising joint action (programmatic). 'Agents' are fictional players (states, firms, people), not necessarily AI. Human validation kappa 0.84 on 30 scenarios; no CIs or multi-seed variance. GitHub causalNLP/gt-harmbench.
